analysis.title: US Equities Weekly Rundown: Positioning, Flows, and Observations Across the Floor (October 2, 2026)
key_insights: The S&P 500 fell 0.3% on the week while the Nasdaq 100 closed at a new all-time high, passing its 6/3 and 9/22 highs. The desk says investors are weighing a weak NFP, an in-line ISM Manufacturing survey and a more demanding macro backdrop of oil, rates and geopolitics.

US fundamental long/short net leverage fell for a third straight week, by 2.2 pts to 46.4%. That is the lowest since April 2025 and in the 2nd percentile of five-year history. Gross leverage fell 1.4 pts to 209.2% and the long/short ratio is at 1.57, in the 1st percentile of five years.

US equities were modestly net bought on the week (+0.4 SDs vs 1 year), driven by short covering in Macro Products (index and ETF combined, the largest net buying in two months). Single stocks were net sold for a second week, with short sales outpacing long buys 1.5 to 1.
8 of 11 US sectors were net sold, led in dollar terms by Comm Svcs, Consumer Discretionary, Materials and Staples. Health Care, Utilities and Financials were the only net bought sectors.

Hedge funds bought US Health Care at the fastest pace in over six months (+1.6 SDs vs 1 year) after six straight weeks of selling. It was almost entirely short covering, and the week's covering was the largest since October 2022 (99th percentile of five years). Biotech, Pharma and Life Sciences Tools led.

Energy was net sold for a sixth straight week even with oil near multi-year highs. It is the most net sold sector on the Prime book over the month (-1.9 SDs), driven by short sales in Refining & Marketing, Oilfield Services and Integrated names. Hedge funds are now 0.4% underweight Energy vs the Russell 3000, against a July peak of 1% overweight.

Asset manager and hedge fund equity flows were balanced. The notable theme was Semis demand on positive catalysts (solid MU earnings, an NVDA buyback increase of $150bn). The desk sees minimal willingness to chase the move higher despite light positioning, with activity spotty on macro, midterm and AI narrative uncertainty.

Equal-weight S&P is down seven straight weeks, which the desk reads as continued concentration in Tech at the expense of other sectors, more pronounced in September. Rates keep drawing the attention, and the desk saw very few buyers of duration when yields backed up to pre-NFP levels.

Russell 2000 started October +1.3% after a -5.4% September. Futures positioning is deeply depressed (systematic exposure in the 7th percentile, record leveraged fund shorts per CFTC data as of 9/22). With 30bp of Fed easing priced through year-end, short covering has started and open interest is down $900 million since 9/29. The desk says a sustained rally needs durable rate relief before end-user length rebuilds.

Gold fell 3.6% on the week as of mid-Friday on strong deferred real rates and the Dollar. The 3-month normalized 25-delta put-call skew rose to a 2-month high (62% 1-year rank) before NFP, while CTA positioning remains relatively short, which leaves less momentum selling if prices keep falling.

Derivatives desk: positioning is depressed across the board, especially in vol, and internals look more washed out than the index. The GS Monetary Policy Factor is at -8, near the bottom of its 30-year range. The desk likes IWM and QQQ upside into Q3 earnings and midterms, with QQQ and IWM implied vols in low percentiles.

The desk traded over 140mm of NDX Dec26 105%/115% up-and-out calls, priced in the 43rd percentile. It also likes NDX over RTY outperformance and NDX upvar. It is watching rising odds of a correlation-1 move higher if rates, oil or macro data keep improving, which would force short covering and chase underweights.

ETF desk: over $1.5 trillion has flowed into US ETFs this year, already above last year's record annual total. The desk expects more than $2 trillion for 2026. SPX is on track to beat RTY seven straight weeks (longest since 2018), MAGS had 12 inflows in 13 sessions, and RSP is on track for seven straight weekly declines.

TLT hit an all-time low this week and is on track for losses on seven straight sessions. Fixed income ETF trading volumes accelerated as the 10-year pushed through 5% this month. Muni bond ETFs are tracking one of their worst months in 20 years while inflows continue on tax-loss harvesting rotations.

Thematic desk: beta has been hurt by higher oil, yields and geopolitical uncertainty and has just come out of one of its most volatile stretches. Beta exposure in the Prime book is around the 83rd to 90th percentile. Friday's softer payroll print lowered yields without raising recession fears, which the desk sees as a tailwind for laggards given weak breadth and light net positioning.

TMT specialists: Semis led (SOX +4% vs NDX +70bps) with a wrong-way pattern in earnings reactions (ACN up, muted MU, JBL fade). NDX's 12-month forward multiple is below its multi-year average, but investors question whether share prices can reflect good earnings and when multiple compression ends.

Financials and Real Estate lagged SPX on rate volatility worries for capital markets activity. Healthcare lagged (XLV -2.8% vs SPY flat) with SMID biotech news flow negative and CVS's distribution contract overhang cleared. Industrials and Materials are held back by Middle East, oil, rates and midterm uncertainty, trading at 1 and 5 year lows vs the market, and the desk expects cyclicals to stay for sale until there is clarity.

Energy specialists keep a 'fade energy' stance on crude upside at current levels and flag possible policy intervention on products, including a diesel export ban or quota that would hit Refining. They are more constructive on Integrated names (US and Canada), which have lagged YTD, are defensive in a pullback and have strong expected 3Q setups in trading and downstream.

sector_views.rationale: Specialists favor fading crude upside and see policy risk on refined products, with near-term downside risk for international-exposed oilfield services. Integrated names are the exception.
The group has lagged YTD, is more defensive in an Energy pullback and has strong expected 3Q setups in trading and downstream.
Investors are in a holding pattern on Middle East, oil, rates and midterms. The desk expects cyclicals to stay for sale until one of these clears.
NDX forward multiple is below its multi-year average and fundamentals are improving, but investors doubt share prices will follow earnings and debate fully re-committing to the AI trade.
Hedge funds covered shorts at a record pace, but SMID biotech news flow is negative and angst remains ahead of Medicare STARs for Managed Care.
Rate volatility raises worries about capital markets activity and cycle position. Focus is shifting to bank earnings roughly 1.5 weeks out.

earnings_insights: Semis demand picked up on positive catalysts including 'solid MU earnings' per the desk, though TMT specialists describe the MU price reaction as muted. No EPS figures are given.
NVDA announced a $150bn buyback increase, cited by the desk as a catalyst for Semis demand.
TMT investors saw wrong-way reactions to earnings this week: ACN to the upside, muted MU, JBL fade.
Q3 earnings season is the next focus. Big banks start roughly 1.5 weeks from October 2. Industrials earnings will pit topline strength against price/cost headwinds and macro uncertainty.
The desk says Q3 estimates are being sharpened ahead of EPS season and thinks the market is underpositioned for tech earnings.

macro_indicators.reading: Described as a weak or softer print, no figure given
macro_indicators.interpretation: Pushed yields lower without being soft enough to spark recession fears, which the desk sees as a tailwind for laggards.
Cited with weak NFP as part of the data digestion that kept the S&P 500 down 0.3% on the week.
Together with NFP it eased rate expectations and sparked Russell 2000 short covering.
Market pricing that supports Russell 2000 short covering, though the desk says durable rate relief is still needed.
Near the bottom of its 30-year range, which the desk reads as heavy policy pessimism already reflected across the macro complex.

crypto_views: Spot-bitcoin ETFs registered 9 consecutive days of inflows totaling more than $3 billion, the largest 9-day haul YTD, with over $6 billion in the past two months.
GS Bitcoin Sensitive basket (GSCBBTC1) fell 5.63% on the week and is up 46.48% YTD. Bitcoin was at 84,424.70, up 0.7% on the week.

Russell 2000 recovery depends on durable rate relief, and without it end-user length cannot rebuild.

Midterm elections and high-velocity AI narrative shifts keep activity spotty and limit willingness to chase the Nasdaq 100 higher.
Cyclicals face price/cost headwinds and macro uncertainty in Q3 earnings, and Industrials trade at 1 and 5 year relative lows.
Concentration in mega-cap Tech leaves breadth weak, with equal-weight S&P down seven straight weeks.
Higher rates and rate volatility could drag on capital markets activity and broader growth, per Financials specialists.

tension_points.bull_case: Softer PCE and NFP eased rate expectations (30bp priced through year-end), futures positioning is deeply depressed (7th percentile, record leveraged fund shorts), and open interest is down $900 million since 9/29.
tension_points.bear_case: Sustained outperformance requires durable relief in rates before end-user length can rebuild, and higher long-end yields, rates volatility and wider credit spreads drove the -5.4% September.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A lack of durable relief in rates, since the desk says sustained Russell 2000 outperformance requires it.

tension_points.bull_case: NDX 12-month forward multiple is below its multi-year average, bottoms-up fundamentals are steady to improving, and the desk thinks the market is underpositioned for tech EPS.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors saw wrong-way reactions to earnings (muted MU, JBL fade) and question whether share prices can reflect good results while the macro backdrop of rates and oil stays difficult.

tension_points.theme: Breadth catch-up vs cyclicals for sale
tension_points.bull_case: Softer payrolls lowered yields without recession fears, and weak breadth with light net positioning leaves room for laggards to catch up, with a possible correlation-1 move higher.
tension_points.bear_case: Industrials trade at 1 and 5 year relative lows and specialists expect cyclicals to stay for sale until the Middle East, oil, rates and midterm uncertainty clears.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If rates, oil or macro data stop improving, the desk's setup for shorts to cover and laggards to catch up weakens.
